entities.summary:
The Organization of American States (OAS), founded in 1948 and headquartered in the Pan American Union Building in Washington, D.C., is the premier regional organisation of the Western Hemisphere. It succeeded earlier Pan-American conferences to promote collective security, democracy norms, and cooperation among American states.

Cold War interventions, human-rights commissions, election observation, and twenty-first-century crises from Haiti to Venezuela tested OAS legitimacy amid U.S. influence critiques and Bolivarian alternatives. Its charter democracy clauses became tools—and flashpoints—of regional politics.

The OAS embodies the long project of inter-American institutionalism and its contested hegemony.
